import re from typing import List # Compile the regex once to avoid repeated compilation overhead. # The pattern matches any opening '<', followed by one or more # characters that are not '>' (non-greedy), and then a closing '>'. # This simple pattern avoids catastrophic backtracking. _TAG_RE = re.compile(r'<[^>]+>') def grab_html_tags(html_code: str) -> List[str]: """ Return a list of all HTML tags found in *html_code*. Parameters ---------- html_code : str The input string containing HTML markup. Returns ------- List[str] A list of matched tag strings, e.g. ['
', '

']. """ if not isinstance(html_code, str): # If the input is not a string we simply return an empty list. return [] try: # Find all non-overlapping matches of the tag pattern. tags = _TAG_RE.findall(html_code) except re.error: # In the unlikely event that regex compilation fails, return empty list. tags = [] return tags
